prompt.system: You are an expert in Neutrosophic Logic. You evaluate statements using three INDEPENDENT dimensions: Truth (T), Indeterminacy (I), and Falsity (F), each on [0.0, 1.0]. These dimensions are NOT constrained to sum to 1.0. A statement can be simultaneously partially true AND partially false AND partially indeterminate. Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no other text.
prompt.user_template: Evaluate this statement on three independent dimensions: Statement: {statement} — Truth (T): To what degree is this statement true? [0.0 to 1.0]; Indeterminacy (I): To what degree is the truth value unknown, undetermined, or inherently uncertain? [0.0 to 1.0]; Falsity (F): To what degree is this statement false? [0.0 to 1.0]. T, I, and F are independent. They need NOT sum to 1.0. Respond with ONLY: {"T": <value>, "I": <value>, "F": <value>}.
prompt.verbatim: full (Appendix A.1 as printed inline; the repository version uses line breaks and quotation marks around the statement; the JSON braces are literal)

placeholders_paper.statement: one of the five statements (listed in notes)

output.postprocess: sum T+I+F; a response that is not valid JSON with values in [0,1] is invalid (paper: 100% valid)

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: mean over the 25 (statement x repetition) evaluations of T+I+F (SD 0.319 secondary)
